title: The context window
blurb: What a model can “see” at once — and why it seems to forget.

slides.title: The context window is the model’s working memory
body: Everything the model can see at once — instructions, your messages, its replies, any pasted documents — has to fit inside one window, measured in tokens.
Anything outside the window simply doesn’t exist for the model.

visual.caption: Everything in one request shares the same window, including space for the reply.

slides.title: It doesn’t remember — it rereads
body: A model keeps no memory between messages. Each time you send something, the app sends the whole conversation again from the top.
That’s why long chats get slower and costlier: the window keeps filling up.

visual.caption: Each new message resends everything that came before it.

slides.title: When it’s full, something has to give
body: Windows are large but finite. When a conversation outgrows one, the app has to drop or summarise older parts.
Details from early on can quietly disappear — the model isn’t ignoring you, it can no longer see them.

visual.caption: In many apps the oldest content is dropped or summarised first.

slides.title: Using context well
body: You control what goes into the window, so a little care goes a long way.

visual.caption: Good habits for any AI chat tool.

items.heading: Give it the source
items.text: Paste the document or facts you want used — don’t assume it knows.

items.heading: Start fresh for new topics
items.text: A clean window stops old details leaking into new answers.

items.heading: Restate what matters
items.text: In long chats, repeat key constraints rather than relying on message one.

quiz.question: What is the context window?
options: The text a model can see at once, measured in tokens
The size of the chat app on your screen
A database of everything you’ve ever typed
The data the model was trained on
quiz.explanation: The context window is the model’s working space for a single request — instructions, conversation and documents together.

quiz.question: You start a brand-new chat. What does the model remember from yesterday’s?
options: Nothing — unless the app adds it to the new context
quiz.explanation: The model itself keeps nothing between requests. Some apps offer “memory” features, but they work by adding saved notes into the context.

quiz.question: A long chat seems to forget an instruction you gave at the start. Most likely cause?
options: The instruction was dropped from, or buried in, a crowded window
The model decided to ignore it
quiz.explanation: Early content can be cut or summarised as the window fills, and even when present it can get lost among lots of later text.
